# Temple Scroll Column 17 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 17 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 17:1 — "multiply wives" vs. "acquire many wives" vs. "take many wives"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "he shall not multiply for himself wives" | Literal lo yarbeh lo nashim |
| LOGOS | "He shall not acquire many wives for himself" | Standard rendering; "acquire" clearer than "multiply" |
| PNEUMA | "The king must not take many wives" | Natural phrasing; specifies "the king" as subject |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Acquire many wives" is the standard rendering of this Deuteronomic prohibition. EMET's "multiply" is archaic. PNEUMA's "take" is acceptable but "acquire" better reflects the political-diplomatic context of royal marriages.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 17:3 — "this torah" vs. "a copy of this law" vs. "a copy of this law"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "this torah" | Preserves the Hebrew term untranslated |
| LOGOS | "a copy of this law" | Mishneh ha-torah rendered as "copy of this law" |
| PNEUMA | "a copy of this law" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "a copy of this law" (LOGOS/PNEUMA). While "torah" is preserved untranslated elsewhere in the project, here the context is specifically the written legal document that the king must copy. "Law" accurately renders torah in this legislative context. "Copy" supplied per Deuteronomy 17:18.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/PNEUMA.

---

## 17:6 — "fear Me" vs. "revere Me" — yare'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "to fear Me" | Literal yir'at; preserves the full force of the Hebrew |
| LOGOS | "to fear Me" | Standard rendering in formal register |
| PNEUMA | "to revere Me" | "Revere" captures respectful awe without implying terror |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "fear Me" (EMET/LOGOS). The yir'ah concept encompasses both awe and dread before the divine presence. "Revere" (PNEUMA) softens the concept unduly — the king is to experience genuine fear of God as a check on royal power.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 17:8 — "heart not lifted up" vs. "heart not exalted" vs. "not thinking he is better"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "his heart shall not be lifted up above his brothers" | Literal levavo lo yarum me-echav |
| LOGOS | "his heart may not be exalted above his brothers" | "Exalted" is more formal; preserves the metaphor |
| PNEUMA | "This will keep him from thinking he is better than his fellow Israelites" | Interpretive; explains the metaphor |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Heart exalted above his brothers" preserves both the cardiac metaphor and the relational language. PNEUMA's "thinking he is better" is an accurate interpretation but loses the Hebrew imagery. EMET's "lifted up" is acceptable but "exalted" has more gravitas.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 17:9 — "prolong his days over/in his kingdom" — preposition choice

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "prolong his days over his kingdom" | Literal al mamlakhto |
| LOGOS | "prolong his days in his kingdom" | "In" more natural in English |
| PNEUMA | "reign long over his kingdom" | Dynamic restructuring |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "in his kingdom" (LOGOS). While al can mean "over," the idiom "prolong days in" is standard in English biblical translation. PNEUMA's restructuring loses the "prolong days" formula.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 17:12 — "anointed with oil" vs. "spread with oil" vs. "coated with oil" — wafer preparation

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "wafers anointed with oil" | Literal meshuchim ba-shemen |
| LOGOS | "wafers spread with oil" | "Spread" describes the culinary action |
| PNEUMA | "wafers coated with oil" | "Coated" implies thorough covering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "spread with oil" (LOGOS). The Hebrew mashach when applied to food items means to smear or spread, not the ritual anointing associated with kings/priests. "Spread" is the most accurate culinary term. EMET's "anointed" imports ritual overtones inappropriate for bread preparation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 17:16 — "bring near" vs. "bring" — spatial verb for approaching the Tent

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "you shall bring near to the entrance of the tent of meeting" | Literal hiqriv el petach ohel mo'ed |
| LOGOS | "You shall bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting" | Standard; "bring to" sufficient |
| PNEUMA | "Then bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting" | Same as LOGOS with informal opener |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Bring to" adequately captures the spatial movement without the awkward "bring near to" (EMET). Capitalized "Tent of Meeting" as a proper noun per all three translators.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
